reviews.text: [quote] 加入[url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/ADZZW#]爱の榨汁屋[/url]&关注[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/34815366/]爱の鉴赏家[/url]，用爱品鉴世间作品，用心流淌真情实感。 [/quote] https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1845811047 《Lost Flame（迷失的火焰）》是一款Roguelike风格的RPG游戏。游戏体量较轻，不过内容和剧情比较丰富。虽然是回合制，但是强调站位和切入战斗的方向，看着简单，还是挺考验运营策略的。另外，由于开始时没有什么教程或者引导，玩家得通过自己的摸索进行挑战，在增加难度的同时也增加了挑战性。不打折时游戏定价47元，有些偏高，不过结合较高的可玩性，喜欢这类游戏的玩家，可以考虑在促销时入手。 https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1845811073 不同于传统的小作坊RPG，这款游戏的战斗系统设置非常严密，在前期较弱的时候，玩家甚至需要针对不同的敌人非常严谨地调整装备部署。另外，还有一些卷轴和药剂可以起到辅助作用，不过同样也需要根据敌人的种类服用。在游戏的城镇中提供大量的信息，建议新玩家早期可以尽快找到一个城镇，在这之后，大量的任务以及游戏世界的背景知识，会为你的游戏找到许多动力和目标。 https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1845811104 此外，游戏的作者非常贴心地考虑到了玩家体验。界面虽然是粗糙的像素风，但是游戏本身设计却不简陋。尤其是背景音乐出奇地很丰富，大多都很好听，甚至适合单独拿出来做一个OST。环境音效和光效也做的很出色，让这样一款看上去很简单的游戏，由于氛围营造的成功，而带来了不少沉浸感。而且，作者还加快了非战斗状态下人物的移动速度，可以说，凡是在游戏核心内容外会造成时间流逝的内容，作者通通有效削减甚至是排除了。 总的来说，喜欢Roguelike风格、像素风的玩家老爷，可以考虑游玩本作体验一下。 [table] [tr] [th]游戏体验[/th] [th]7/10[/th] [/tr] [tr] [td]上手难度[/td] [td]7/10[/td] [/tr] [tr] [td]质量水准[/td] [td]6/10[/td] [/tr] [tr] [td]推荐程度[/td] [td]6/10[/td]

THE BEST ROGUELIKE ON STEAM Seriously a hidden gem. The amount of depth and replayability after the latest updates are incredible. There are no other grid-based roguelikes that offer this level of depth while also being streamlined and unique. To top it off, Lost Flame has the best movement/combat system in the genre and has expansive character/build customization options that offer hours of playtime in the triple digits.
This seems really good, and I hope it's not abandoned. Edited: It wasn't abandoned, and is even better now. :3c

Edit: The dev made it where the numpad can be used to navigate the menu which is a welcome change and should be standard in all rogue-likes (looking at you Jupiter Hell.....). There's one other small issue, every time I boot up the game I have to select fullscreen, it'd be nice if it didn't default back to windowed every time I launch the game. Sill really enjoying the game, this is easily up there next to Caves of Qud for me as far as modern masterpieces of rogue-likes--I really enjoy how the game is very approachable without a ton of knowledge of the game like some older rogue-likes such as Nethack or ADoM. From what I've played so far I really like the game and it has a ton of promise. Skills depend on your weapon loadout, most attacks are telegraphed, it's a pretty fun game. I only have a few things to note: 1) When I first launched the game on both my desktop and laptop for the first time my inventory was opened and could not be closed. After closing the game and relaunching it I didn't experience it again, but I did see it on both desktop and laptop the first time I booted it up on either. 2) Multi-tile enemy AI can be kinda dumb when trying to get through a door, I've had instances where they should walk up or down a tile or two to go through a door to get to me but won't unless I move in that direction 3) Huge pet peeve of mine though it should be simple to fix, sometimes the numpad cannot navigate through a menu and I have to use the arrow keys like the starting screen, it'd be really nice to be able to use the numpad there too Other than those three minor issues this game shows a lot of promise :)

It's a shame this game isn't more well known. It's one of the most polished and innovative roguelikes on Steam. To the developer: it would be nice if you offered alternative saving options. The game has crashed for me ~3 times during streaming and I've lost progress each time. Because this game deletes the save file when the game is loaded, and it only recreates it when you click "Save & Exit" (vs whenever a bonfire is used), _all_ progress gets lost immediately. It is very disheartening. EDIT: Changing this review to a Negative since the developer never fixed the save mechanics. Game still crashes, progress still gets wiped. Really poor player experience.

黑魂风味的传统RL，翻滚走位，利用武器特征和敌人周旋，找机会弹反敌人（然后没弹到原地被晕一回合）。比较有特色的就是需要管理耐力系统，有一大堆各种各样奇怪属性的戒指，需要你根据情况搭配，而且不同装备用附魔卷轴还会强化特有词条，还算有些特色。整个流程不长，最简单的结局两三个小时就能打通（但是其他结局每个都很麻烦)。初见杀非常多，石化、被变成青蛙踩死、被一堆法师把包里的卷轴都烧了、被触手包围扒光身上装备惨死。作为传统RL，游戏本身提供一命模式、有限生命模式(还有作弊模式)。 总而言之是个黑魂风味、有些特色的传统RL，RL爱好者可以尝试下。

It's been a long time since a traditional roguelike came out that was original in some way. Combat in this game is superior to the standard "bump or run" combat of the genre greats. Game like DCSS and bRogue are still excellent games, but Lost Flame joins their ranks as one with evolved combat. All the elements of Angband are here: massive library of items, fog of war dungeons, scrolls of identify, etc. I will be playing this one for many hours to come. It's in the weapon items that the game shines. Each different type of weapon comes with a different set of moves, such as tumble, parry, lunge, etc. I am enjoying my named spear, 'Protector', at the moment. It allows me to skewer two enemies in one turn. There are [b]many[/b] named items in the game - if you're a loot junkie like me, you're in for a treat. There is also live chat, ToME-style. There isn't a lot of conversation yet, but deaths and level-ups abound. I'm not sure if it can be toggled on/off (probably), but it's not intrusive so I haven't sought out that function. 9/10 - Strong recommendation.
Innovative to the format, extremely fun and addictive, many secrets, the dedication put into making this game really shows.
Very good traditional roguelike with a lot of secrets and pretty fun combat. Definitely has the feeling of a Souls atmosphere despite being turn-based. Highly recommend and good difficulty as well.
Good job dev, amazing game! It's accessible, fast and has great controls. My favorite steamdeck game at the moment.

Still intending to play a lot more, but for now leaving a positive review to help support visibility and just because the game is pretty great as far as traditional roguelikes go. Almost everything about it feels good and it has a lot of innovation and good mechanics taken from other places in the genre. Main complaints so far would be: Items being destroyed during combat happens A LOT - namely losing potions to ice damage, and scrolls to fire (thank heck acid eroding/destroying armour/weapons doesn't seem to also be a thing). There are ways to preserve your items, but for the most part this just isn't a good feeling mechanic in any game it shows up in - here it's particularly frustrating because the only way to know an item has just been destroyed is by reading it in the combat text log, wherein it's the same colour text and potentially just one line within 15 lines of text for what happened in the last turn (when fighting a lot of enemies this is common.) If this is a balance mechanic to stop players becoming fantasy batman with an arsenal of solutions to problems, then personally I'd rather the balance was done via less items dropping in general - rather than having to account for the risk of enemies that can passively destroy your items. Controller support is good enough to play, but could definitely be better tuned to work with input systems other than steamdeck - currently using an xbox controller via pc, you can't use L3 or R3 to map to something useful like swap weapon set and Look command, which by default are fiddly to access via controller. Having L2 as diagonal input modifier seems like a niche choice, as it feels better to play using left analog and r2 to move versus playing very directional pad + L2 hold for diagonals. L2 being a modifier button would be a good move tho - e.g. L2 + X swaps weapon, L2 + Y uses Spirit Phial, L2+B is tumble, L2 + A is look command - L2 + dpad directions then being mappable to other functions, maybe just autorun in direction (as movement via left analog and r2 is quite slow for navigating a large already mapped level, to look for potential secret paths/non magical loot once autoexplore is exhausted). Also no warning that 'using' a scroll to see what items it's function can be applied to, and then backing out of the item selection screen, will waste the scroll - IMO it's much better QoL for new players if scrolls which target inventory to can be opened and closed without wasting their use.

Soulsy classical roguelike with lots of interesting design decisions, e.g. levelling up identifies and recharges items, including an Estus-Flask-esque healing item. Very interesting tactical combat and diverse item-based builds. I haven’t played a ton yet, but thus far this feels to me like a top-tier combat-focused roguelike.

The flavor text on the enemies is well written. There is world building narrative. My only regret is that I did not discover this game earlier. The controls are a bit awkward but I quickly got used to it. It was pretty funny accidentally drinking a potion of fire twice in a row.

dark souls as a traditional roguelike

This is a pretty solid 'traditional' roguelike. The combat mechanics are a big step up from bump attacks, tons of interesting enemies to use them on, and pretty diverse builds to change up each run. It also I think manages something that many roguelikes struggle with: balancing randomization with planning. What I mean here is most of your build and choices are going to be determined by what you find and when, but you can exert some level of control over this with two things: essences and witchglass. The former is like the boss souls that you can exchange for set items/spells in Souls games, while the latter can be invested into a unique to upgrade that specific unique with new abilities. Each unique can have three applied and has its own progression, so you can specialize around certain drops to direct your own build. Having done a number of runs but not beaten it yet, I would say there are a few minor design decisions I think detract rather than add to the game, but the only major sticking point I have is the decision to have unblocked damage drain your stamina. I get what they are going for; positioning and avoiding damage is key, but there is so much damage flying around, the damage-to-drain-stamina rate is so high, and stamina recovery is so slow that you'll often end up at 0 stamina and be unable to do your cool moves. There are a number of items that can help mitigate this, but there are limited slots making it a big burden to do so. Health already doesn't autorecover making getting hit punishing; I don't think limiting your Cool Moves Meter adds anything to the mix. Aside from that one point, Lost Flame is a great entry into the 'traditional' roguelike genre. If you enjoy Caves of Qud, ToME4, DCSS, and others, you'll definitely want to pick this up at some point.
